key_insight: Three joint-embedding predictive formulations trained stably on longitudinal EHRs but consistently underperformed standard masked language modelling.
clinical_relevance: Stable latent-space learning alone did not yield competitive patient representations in this study, limiting its promise for downstream clinical AI tasks.
method: Adapted three Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) formulations to longitudinal EHR sequences.
Compared latent-representation prediction with masked language modelling.
Examined how target size and heterogeneity affected prediction error.
evidence_signal: In MIMIC-IV experiments, all three JEPA formulations avoided representational collapse, but reducing target size did not recover downstream performance.
watch_item: Results from MIMIC-IV may not generalize to other EHR settings; defining clinically meaningful latent targets remains a challenge.
paper_title: Are Joint-Embedding Predictive Objectives Effective for Longitudinal EHRs?
